Use only the status field with UNKNOWN, SUSPECTED, KNOWN, or FORGOTTEN; leave the generic state field null. In character_belief_changes, use only stance with BELIEVES, DOUBTS, DISBELIEVES, or UNCERTAIN plus belief_confidence from zero to one; use from_stance only for an exact accepted baseline and leave generic state, status, from_state, and from_status null. In relationship_changes, always copy both directed graph endpoints into source_id and target_id; entity_id cannot replace an endpoint, and the generic character_id field must remain null. Use obligation_changes for the unified accepted Narrative Obligation lifecycle. Copy obligation_id, obligation_type, priority, target_window, and linked Arc identities from governed context. FULFILLED requires a typed payoff_evidence object naming the accepted draft AssetVersion and the supported payoff event; Arc evidence alone never silently closes an obligation. For CAUSAL_DEBT, preserve causal_plan_asset_version_id and the exact causal_requirement.payload_json predicate from its planning origin. A plan cannot repay debt: FULFILLED requires a satisfied condition and its accepted source event as payoff_evidence.event_id. Other obligation types use null for these two causal fields. World, faction, location, consequence and conflict state changes require world_transition.payload_json: transition_id, actor_id, camera (ON_CAMERA, OFF_CAMERA or UNDERCURRENT), native StoryTime, action, state_kind, exact entity_key, changes, requirements, cause_refs and epistemic_basis. Causes must resolve to accepted source events. Observe only events supported by the final prose, including explicitly narrated off-camera events; a proposed future is not an occurrence. Every typed change must copy its exact stable Authority identity: character_id for character and power state, event_id for timeline, thread_id for foreshadow and plot thread, promise_id, reward_id, rule_id, entity_id plus resource_id for resource balances, fingerprint_id, antagonist_id, character_id plus arc_id for character trajectory, arc_id for narrative Arc state, and disclosure_id for presentation. A generic entity_id never substitutes for another domain's identity. If no stable identity is available in governed context, omit the unsupported change. Emit every supported planned non-WITHHOLD presentation as a disclosure_event, including character-facing events; accepted reader-facing Disclosure alone is deterministically projected into Reader Knowledge. Record how the information was presented through disclosure_mode, audience, and presentation_channel rather than copying Truth into every epistemic layer. Reconcile the frozen execution_expectations exactly. For every required state transition supported by the chapter, emit one change in the corresponding typed array with the exact planned identity and to_state; do not paraphrase either. Omit from_* only when the governed context has no accepted baseline. For every planned disclosure, copy disclosure_id, fact_id, audience, and mode exactly; do not expand the audience. Reader Knowledge will be derived after the Disclosure is accepted. Arc and Narrative Realization evidence describes Actual accepted prose, never Plan or Future Intent. Return exactly one arc_evidence item for each frozen expected Arc contribution. Use observation_status OBSERVED only when the accepted revision visibly executes that contribution. An OBSERVED Arc item must include at least one resolution_evidence string encoded as chars:<start>-<end>:<summary>, where start and end are valid character offsets into accepted_revision; otherwise return zero progress_units and an empty resolution_evidence list. Return one realization_evidence item for every frozen Narrative Realization event. OBSERVED realization evidence requires a non-empty accepted_prose_evidence list with valid accepted_revision character offsets plus the observed event identity, action, decision, consequence, and state deltas. Planning context alone never proves observation. Within canon_facts, each (subject, predicate, impact_type) tuple may occur at most once. When one subject has multiple objects for a broad relation, either combine them into one object when they are one bundled fact, or use precise relation-specific predicates. For example, encode separate consent facts as authorizes_testimony and authorizes_public_identification instead of repeating authorizes with two objects. Never emit two different objects for the same semantic tuple. Use resource_state_changes only for quantifiable resource balances. An initial resource baseline must set balance_after; a later transition must set balance_before, delta, and balance_after with exact arithmetic. Do not encode custody, location, protection, ownership, or other qualitative object status as a Resource State merely because the object is a story resource; represent supported qualitative changes as precise canon_facts or timeline_events instead. If the prose supplies no numeric balance, leave resource_state_changes only facts and state changes supported by the revised chapter. Treat from_status, from_state, from_stance, and from_tier only as compare-and-set preconditions against the exact accepted Story State supplied in the governed context. For a first occurrence with no accepted entity baseline, leave from_status, from_state, from_stance, and from_tier null; never infer them from prose, Story Design assets, plans, or ordinary background conditions. For canon_facts, compare each (subject, predicate) slot with the accepted Canon facts supplied in the governed context. If the chapter does not materially change an accepted fact, omit the redundant fact or reuse its object exactly. If the chapter changes, refines, or replaces that fact, copy the accepted fact's exact source_event_id into supersedes_event_id. Never paraphrase an unchanged accepted fact into a different object, and never invent a supersession identity. Treat requires_fact_ids as character-specific epistemic preconditions. Every required fact must already appear in that character's accepted known facts in the governed context, or the chapter must first establish it through an atomic character_knowledge_changes item with fact_id and chapter evidence. World-rule availability is not automatically character knowledge. If the prose and governed context do not establish the knowledge, omit the unsupported action or requirement; never add unsupported knowledge merely to satisfy validation. Keep Story Truth, Character Knowledge, Character Belief, Reader Knowledge, and presentation separate: a Canon fact does not by itself make any character or the reader aware of it; a belief may be false. In character_knowledge_changes, emit one item per character_id plus fact_id or proposition_id; never bundle multiple newly learned facts into one Character Knowledge event. Use only the status field with UNKNOWN, SUSPECTED, KNOWN, or FORGOTTEN; leave the generic state field null. In character_belief_changes, use only stance with BELIEVES, DOUBTS, DISBELIEVES, or UNCERTAIN plus belief_confidence from zero to one; use from_stance only for an exact accepted baseline and leave generic state, status, from_state, and from_status null. In relationship_changes, always copy both directed graph endpoints into source_id and target_id; entity_id cannot replace an endpoint, and the generic character_id field must remain null. Use obligation_changes for the unified accepted Narrative Obligation lifecycle. Copy obligation_id, obligation_type, priority, target_window, and linked Arc identities from governed context. FULFILLED requires a typed payoff_evidence object naming the accepted draft AssetVersion and the supported payoff event; Arc evidence alone never silently closes an obligation. For CAUSAL_DEBT, preserve causal_plan_asset_version_id and the exact causal_requirement.payload_json predicate from its planning origin. A plan cannot repay debt: FULFILLED requires a satisfied condition and its accepted source event as payoff_evidence.event_id. Other obligation types use null for these two causal fields. World, faction, location, consequence and conflict state changes require world_transition.payload_json: transition_id, actor_id, camera (ON_CAMERA, OFF_CAMERA or UNDERCURRENT), native StoryTime, action, state_kind, exact entity_key, changes, requirements, cause_refs and epistemic_basis. Causes must resolve to accepted source events. Observe only events supported by the final prose, including explicitly narrated off-camera events; a proposed future is not an occurrence. Every typed change must copy its exact stable Authority identity: character_id for character and power state, event_id for timeline, thread_id for foreshadow and plot thread, promise_id, reward_id, rule_id, entity_id plus resource_id for resource balances, fingerprint_id, antagonist_id, character_id plus arc_id for character trajectory, arc_id for narrative Arc state, and disclosure_id for presentation. A generic entity_id never substitutes for another domain's identity. If no stable identity is available in governed context, omit the unsupported change. Emit every supported planned non-WITHHOLD presentation as a disclosure_event, including character-facing events; accepted reader-facing Disclosure alone is deterministically projected into Reader Knowledge. Record how the information was presented through disclosure_mode, audience, and presentation_channel rather than copying Truth into every epistemic layer. Reconcile the frozen execution_expectations exactly. For every required state transition supported by the chapter, emit one change in the corresponding typed array with the exact planned identity and to_state; do not paraphrase either. Omit from_* only when the governed context has no accepted baseline. For every planned disclosure, copy disclosure_id, fact_id, audience, and mode exactly; do not expand the audience. Reader Knowledge will be derived after the Disclosure is accepted. Arc and Narrative Realization evidence describes Actual accepted prose, never Plan or Future Intent. Return exactly one arc_evidence item for each frozen expected Arc contribution. Use observation_status OBSERVED only when the accepted revision visibly executes that contribution. An OBSERVED Arc item must include at least one resolution_evidence string encoded as chars:<start>-<end>:<summary>, where start and end are valid character offsets into accepted_revision; otherwise return zero progress_units and an empty resolution_evidence list. Return one realization_evidence item for every frozen Narrative Realization event. OBSERVED realization evidence requires a non-empty accepted_prose_evidence list with valid accepted_revision character offsets plus the observed event identity, action, decision, consequence, and state deltas. Planning context alone never proves observation. Within canon_facts, each (subject, predicate, impact_type) tuple may occur at most once. When one subject has multiple objects for a broad relation, either combine them into one object when they are one bundled fact, or use precise relation-specific predicates. For example, encode separate consent facts as authorizes_testimony and authorizes_public_identification instead of repeating authorizes with two objects. Never emit two different objects for the same semantic tuple. Use resource_state_changes only for quantifiable resource balances. An initial resource baseline must set balance_after; a later transition must set balance_before, delta, and balance_after with exact arithmetic. Do not encode custody, location, protection, ownership, or other qualitative object status as a Resource State merely because the object is a story resource; represent supported qualitative changes as precise canon_facts or timeline_events instead. If the prose supplies no numeric balance, leave resource_state_changes output schema: schema:chapter-provider-output:canon_extraction:v15\nReturn only the schema-backed stage result and its evidence references.\n\n</prompt_template>\n\n<stage_semantic_contract>\nExtract only facts and state changes supported by the revised chapter. Treat from_status, from_state, from_stance, and from_tier only as compare-and-set preconditions against the exact accepted Story State supplied in the governed context. For a first occurrence with no accepted entity baseline, leave from_status, from_state, from_stance, and from_tier null; never infer them from prose, Story Design assets, plans, or ordinary background conditions. For canon_facts, compare each (subject, predicate) slot with the accepted Canon facts supplied in the governed context. If the chapter does not materially change an accepted fact, omit the redundant fact or reuse its object exactly. If the chapter changes, refines, or replaces that fact, copy the accepted fact's exact source_event_id into supersedes_event_id. Never paraphrase an unchanged accepted fact into a different object, and never invent a supersession identity. Treat requires_fact_ids as character-specific epistemic preconditions. Every required fact must already appear in that character's accepted known facts in the governed context, or the chapter must first establish it through an atomic character_knowledge_changes item with fact_id and chapter evidence. World-rule availability is not automatically character knowledge. If the prose and governed context do not establish the knowledge, omit the unsupported action or requirement; never add unsupported knowledge merely to satisfy validation. Keep Story Truth, Character Knowledge, Character Belief, Reader Knowledge, and presentation separate: a Canon fact does not by itself make any character or the reader aware of it; a belief may be false. In character_knowledge_changes, emit one item per character_id plus fact_id or proposition_id; never bundle multiple newly learned facts into one Character Knowledge event. Use only the status field with UNKNOWN, SUSPECTED, KNOWN, or FORGOTTEN; leave the generic state field null. In character_belief_changes, use only stance with BELIEVES, DOUBTS, DISBELIEVES, or UNCERTAIN plus belief_confidence from zero to one; use from_stance only for an exact accepted baseline and leave generic state, status, from_state, and from_status null. In relationship_changes, always copy both directed graph endpoints into source_id and target_id; entity_id cannot replace an endpoint, and the generic character_id field must remain null. Use obligation_changes for the unified accepted Narrative Obligation lifecycle. Copy obligation_id, obligation_type, priority, target_window, and linked Arc identities from governed context. FULFILLED requires a typed payoff_evidence object naming the accepted draft AssetVersion and the supported payoff event; Arc evidence alone never silently closes an obligation. For CAUSAL_DEBT, preserve causal_plan_asset_version_id and the exact causal_requirement.payload_json predicate from its planning origin. A plan cannot repay debt: FULFILLED requires a satisfied condition and its accepted source event as payoff_evidence.event_id. Other obligation types use null for these two causal fields. World, faction, location, consequence and conflict state changes require world_transition.payload_json: transition_id, actor_id, camera (ON_CAMERA, OFF_CAMERA or UNDERCURRENT), native StoryTime, action, state_kind, exact entity_key, changes, requirements, cause_refs and epistemic_basis. Causes must resolve to accepted source events. Observe only events supported by the final prose, including explicitly narrated off-camera events; a proposed future is not an occurrence. Every typed change must copy its exact stable Authority identity: character_id for character and power state, event_id for timeline, thread_id for foreshadow and plot thread, promise_id, reward_id, rule_id, entity_id plus resource_id for resource balances, fingerprint_id, antagonist_id, character_id plus arc_id for character trajectory, arc_id for narrative Arc state, and disclosure_id for presentation. A generic entity_id never substitutes for another domain's identity. If no stable identity is available in governed context, omit the unsupported change. Emit every supported planned non-WITHHOLD presentation as a disclosure_event, including character-facing events; accepted reader-facing Disclosure alone is deterministically projected into Reader Knowledge. Record how the information was presented through disclosure_mode, audience, and presentation_channel rather than copying Truth into every epistemic layer. Reconcile the frozen execution_expectations exactly. For every required state transition supported by the chapter, emit one change in the corresponding typed array with the exact planned identity and to_state; do not paraphrase either. Omit from_* only when the governed context has no accepted baseline. For every planned disclosure, copy disclosure_id, fact_id, audience, and mode exactly; do not expand the audience. Reader Knowledge will be derived after the Disclosure is accepted. Arc and Narrative Realization evidence describes Actual accepted prose, never Plan or Future Intent. Return exactly one arc_evidence item for each frozen expected Arc contribution. Use observation_status OBSERVED only when the accepted revision visibly executes that contribution. An OBSERVED Arc item must include at least one resolution_evidence string encoded as chars:<start>-<end>:<summary>, where start and end are valid character offsets into accepted_revision; otherwise return zero progress_units and an empty resolution_evidence list. Return one realization_evidence item for every frozen Narrative Realization event. OBSERVED realization evidence requires a non-empty accepted_prose_evidence list with valid accepted_revision character offsets plus the observed event identity, action, decision, consequence, and state deltas. Planning context alone never proves observation. Within canon_facts, each (subject, predicate, impact_type) tuple may occur at most once. When one subject has multiple objects for a broad relation, either combine them into one object when they are one bundled fact, or use precise relation-specific predicates. Do not encode custody, location, protection, ownership, or other qualitative object status as a Resource State merely because the object is a story resource; represent supported qualitative changes as precise canon_facts or timeline_events instead. only facts and state changes supported by the revised chapter. Treat from_status, from_state, from_stance, and from_tier only as compare-and-set preconditions against the exact accepted Story State supplied in the governed context. For a first occurrence with no accepted entity baseline, leave from_status, from_state, from_stance, and from_tier null; never infer them from prose, Story Design assets, plans, or ordinary background conditions. For canon_facts, compare each (subject, predicate) slot with the accepted Canon facts supplied in the governed context. If the chapter does not materially change an accepted fact, omit the redundant fact or reuse its object exactly. If the chapter changes, refines, or replaces that fact, copy the accepted fact's exact source_event_id into supersedes_event_id. Never paraphrase an unchanged accepted fact into a different object, and never invent a supersession identity. Treat requires_fact_ids as character-specific epistemic preconditions. Every required fact must already appear in that character's accepted known facts in the governed context, or the chapter must first establish it through an atomic character_knowledge_changes item with fact_id and chapter evidence. World-rule availability is not automatically character knowledge. If the prose and governed context do not establish the knowledge, omit the unsupported action or requirement; never add unsupported knowledge merely to satisfy validation. Keep Story Truth, Character Knowledge, Character Belief, Reader Knowledge, and presentation separate: a Canon fact does not by itself make any character or the reader aware of it; a belief may be false. In character_knowledge_changes, emit one item per character_id plus fact_id or proposition_id; never bundle multiple newly learned facts into one Character Knowledge event. Use only the status field with UNKNOWN, SUSPECTED, KNOWN, or FORGOTTEN; leave the generic state field null. In character_belief_changes, use only stance with BELIEVES, DOUBTS, DISBELIEVES, or UNCERTAIN plus belief_confidence from zero to one; use from_stance only for an exact accepted baseline and leave generic state, status, from_state, and from_status null. In relationship_changes, always copy both directed graph endpoints into source_id and target_id; entity_id cannot replace an endpoint, and the generic character_id field must remain null. Use obligation_changes for the unified accepted Narrative Obligation lifecycle. Copy obligation_id, obligation_type, priority, target_window, and linked Arc identities from governed context. FULFILLED requires a typed payoff_evidence object naming the accepted draft AssetVersion and the supported payoff event; Arc evidence alone never silently closes an obligation. For CAUSAL_DEBT, preserve causal_plan_asset_version_id and the exact causal_requirement.payload_json predicate from its planning origin. A plan cannot repay debt: FULFILLED requires a satisfied condition and its accepted source event as payoff_evidence.event_id. Other obligation types use null for these two causal fields. World, faction, location, consequence and conflict state changes require world_transition.payload_json: transition_id, actor_id, camera (ON_CAMERA, OFF_CAMERA or UNDERCURRENT), native StoryTime, action, state_kind, exact entity_key, changes, requirements, cause_refs and epistemic_basis. Causes must resolve to accepted source events. Observe only events supported by the final prose, including explicitly narrated off-camera events; a proposed future is not an occurrence. Every typed change must copy its exact stable Authority identity: character_id for character and power state, event_id for timeline, thread_id for foreshadow and plot thread, promise_id, reward_id, rule_id, entity_id plus resource_id for resource balances, fingerprint_id, antagonist_id, character_id plus arc_id for character trajectory, arc_id for narrative Arc state, and disclosure_id for presentation. A generic entity_id never substitutes for another domain's identity. If no stable identity is available in governed context, omit the unsupported change. Emit every supported planned non-WITHHOLD presentation as a disclosure_event, including character-facing events; accepted reader-facing Disclosure alone is deterministically projected into Reader Knowledge. Record how the information was presented through disclosure_mode, audience, and presentation_channel rather than copying Truth into every epistemic layer. Reconcile the frozen execution_expectations exactly. For every required state transition supported by the chapter, emit one change in the corresponding typed array with the exact planned identity and to_state; do not paraphrase either. Omit from_* only when the governed context has no accepted baseline. For every planned disclosure, copy disclosure_id, fact_id, audience, and mode exactly; do not expand the audience. Reader Knowledge will be derived after the Disclosure is accepted. Arc and Narrative Realization evidence describes Actual accepted prose, never Plan or Future Intent. Return exactly one arc_evidence item for each frozen expected Arc contribution. Use observation_status OBSERVED only when the accepted revision visibly executes that contribution. An OBSERVED Arc item must include at least one resolution_evidence string encoded as chars:<start>-<end>:<summary>, where start and end are valid character offsets into accepted_revision; otherwise return zero progress_units and an empty resolution_evidence list. Return one realization_evidence item for every frozen Narrative Realization event. OBSERVED realization evidence requires a non-empty accepted_prose_evidence list with valid accepted_revision character offsets plus the observed event identity, action, decision, consequence, and state deltas. Planning context alone never proves observation. Within canon_facts, each (subject, predicate, impact_type) tuple may occur at most once. When one subject has multiple objects for a broad relation, either combine them into one object when they are one bundled fact, or use precise relation-specific predicates. For example, encode separate consent facts as authorizes_testimony and authorizes_public_identification instead of repeating authorizes with two objects. Never emit two different objects for the same semantic tuple. Use resource_state_changes only for quantifiable resource balances. An initial resource baseline must set balance_after; a later transition must set balance_before, delta, and balance_after with exact arithmetic. Do not encode custody, location, protection, ownership, or other qualitative object status as a Resource State merely because the object is a story resource; represent supported qualitative changes as precise canon_facts or timeline_events instead. If the prose supplies no numeric balance, leave resource_state_changes
